root_cause.text: The genpd detach path in the PM domain core failed to symmetrically undo runtime PM setup for genpd-created virtual devices, leaving runtime PM enabled after detachment and allowing later genpd runtime callbacks to operate on a detached device state.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit explicitly state that genpd_dev_pm_attach_by_id() calls pm_runtime_enable() for registered virtual devices, but genpd_dev_pm_detach() had “no corresponding call to pm_runtime_disable()”; the patch adds an is_virt_dev check and calls pm_runtime_disable(dev) before unregistering the virtual device.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local boolean in genpd_dev_pm_detach() to support forthcoming logic for handling virtual devices.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable named is_virt_dev was added to the function genpd_dev_pm_detach(), alongside the existing local variables pd, i, and ret.
intent_record.how: At runtime this change alone has no effect, because it only introduces a variable declaration without any shown initialization or use in the provided diff hunk; it prepares the function for subsequent logic that may distinguish virtual devices.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable runtime PM during genpd detach for genpd-created virtual devices to correctly undo attach-time PM setup.
intent_record.what: The change adds a check in genpd_dev_pm_detach() to detect whether the device is a virtual device created by genpd by comparing dev->bus to &genpd_bus_type, stores the result in is_virt_dev, and conditionally calls pm_runtime_disable(dev) before dropping the default performance state.
intent_record.how: At detach time, devices that were created by genpd during attach now have runtime PM explicitly disabled, preventing runtime PM from remaining enabled after removal from the PM domain and avoiding incorrect power-management state for those virtual devices.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the virtual-device flag instead of a bus-type comparison when deciding whether to unregister a genpd-created device during detach.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding device_unregister(dev) in genpd_dev_pm_detach() was changed from checking whether dev->bus equals &genpd_bus_type to checking the boolean variable is_virt_dev.
intent_record.how: At runtime, device unregistration now depends on the precomputed virtual-device status instead of the bus type pointer comparison, ensuring detach only unregisters devices identified as genpd-created virtual devices and avoiding incorrect unregister decisions based solely on dev->bus.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix genpd detach handling for genpd-created virtual devices by correctly identifying those devices and undoing the runtime PM and registration setup performed at attach time.

relevance_review.reason: The change is in genpd_dev_pm_detach() and specifically introduces state to handle virtual devices, which are central to the root cause involving improper runtime PM teardown for genpd-created virtual devices during detach.

The changes directly fix the detach-path asymmetry described in the root cause: they disable runtime PM for genpd-created virtual devices during detach and correctly identify/unregister those virtual devices, undoing the attach-time setup that otherwise left detached devices with runtime PM still enabled.

candidates.rationale: The detach path used a bus-type check to identify genpd-created virtual devices, but failed to symmetrically undo the runtime PM setup done at attach time. This incorrect/insufficient identification logic is directly tied to mishandling virtual devices during detach and allowed runtime PM to remain enabled on detached devices.

The detach path only unregistered the genpd-created virtual device, but did not first disable runtime PM for it. As a result, the device could later be subject to runtime PM/genpd callbacks after detach, which is the core vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This detach-path statement unregisters the genpd-created virtual device without first undoing the runtime PM enable/setup established during attach. That leaves runtime PM active on a detached device state, enabling later genpd runtime callbacks and directly causing the vulnerability.

This condition was used to identify genpd-created virtual devices in the detach path, but the logic was insufficient for properly handling the full symmetric teardown required for those devices. Its use is directly associated with the faulty detach handling that omitted runtime PM disable before unregister.

PM / Domains: Add support for multi PM domains per device to genpd

To support devices being partitioned across multiple
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the detach/removal path and the handling for genpd-created virtual devices. The root cause says the bug is that detach failed to symmetrically undo runtime PM setup for genpd-created virtual devices, leaving runtime PM enabled. In this snippet, after successful removal from the PM domain, the only cleanup for a genpd-created device is: `if (dev->bus == &genpd_bus_type) device_unregister(dev);` (lines 2221-2223). There is no runtime PM teardown such as disabling runtime PM, clearing active state, or otherwise undoing runtime PM initialization before unregistering the virtual device. That means the vulnerable construct is present: the detach path unregisters the genpd-created device without symmetrically undoing runtime PM setup. Therefore `has_bug` is true and `is_fixed` is false.
